source.entry: Markdown file or directory containing report.md/index.md

directiveSyntax.nestedContainer: Use a longer outer colon fence than nested directives.
directiveSyntax.numericColonText: A colon that opens a digit-initial name, and a colon written against the preceding word, remain literal Markdown text: 21:01, 1:30:05, 3:1, 1:10:100, localhost:9000, ключ:значение and Пункт :2. Only the inline form without attributes or children is restored: a spaced unknown alphabetic name, any attributed or child-bearing form, and every block-level form stay directives; write \: for ordinary prose.

terms.description: Annotates exact first canonical glossary occurrences in one code fence.

eyebrow.description: A short small-caps line above the title that follows it, in the eyebrow colour of the theme; written first in a section, it stands above the section title.

section.description: Labelled top-level page section containing Markdown.

recipe.description: High-level package-owned section composition; explicit detailed attributes override its roles.

place.description: Where the section stands: in the flow of the page, or as the first screen beside the page title (only the first section).

composition.description: Semantic arrangement for the section content; authored reading order is unchanged.

viewport.description: Bounded use of the available viewport without changing document order.

section-density.description: Section-local content rhythm independent of the page density token.

media.description: Art direction for confined local images inside the section.

media-fit.description: Section-local object fitting for confined images.

media-aspect.description: Section-local aspect ratio for confined images.

focal.description: Package-owned object position for cropped local media.

surface.description: Package-owned band behind the section: none, a one-colour tint, a fine grain, a drafting grid, or a blueprint grid with major and minor lines in the accent colour.

frame.description: Section edge: a full-width band with no border, or a bordered rounded panel. browser puts the first picture of the section in a browser window whose bar shows the real address (address) or, for a mock-up, the label Illustration (illustration="true").

address.description: The real address of the page in the picture, shown in the bar of frame="browser": an absolute http or https URL.

illustration.description: The picture in frame="browser" is a mock-up, not a real page: its bar says Illustration.

transition.description: Bounded package-owned entrance treatment: one section reveal, children in turn, the section title line by line, or log: every code block of the section prints line by line like a log, with its whole text in the page from the start; clip opens the chapter from its lower edge; staged, on the first screen (place="opening") only, brings in the page title by lines, then the eyebrow, the subtitle, the actions and the scene.

scene.description: Content-driven scroll scene without changing document order; steps pins the section media while its beats scroll past and switches the picture, the lit part of the diagram or the lit code lines with each beat; scrub pins the media for one screen per beat (two to four) and plays the beats as a timeline of the scroll.

slide-transition.description: How this slide arrives in a presentation (layout slides): a fade, a push, a wipe, a zoom, or at once; the duration is fixed and published.

choreography.description: Semantic ordered emphasis for metrics and visualizations.

reveal.description: Enables one package-owned one-time section reveal in the normal-motion profile.

state.description: Page state set while the reader has reached this section (its top passed the middle of the screen) and cleared when they scroll back above it; blocks with the same when light.

incompatibleCombinations.message: section composition mosaic or stack cannot be combined with layered or gallery media.
incompatibleCombinations.remediation: Use composition flow, stage, split, or story with layered/gallery media, or use natural, mask, or bleed media with mosaic/stack composition.

incompatibleCombinations.message: Layered media cannot also own a pointer transform.
incompatibleCombinations.remediation: Use interaction="none" with layered media or another media treatment.

incompatibleCombinations.message: A progress scene and pointer interaction cannot transform the same media.
incompatibleCombinations.remediation: Use either scene="progress" or a depth/tilt interaction.

incompatibleCombinations.message: Story and stack compositions already own sticky positioning.
incompatibleCombinations.remediation: Use scene="none|progress" or a flow, stage, split, or mosaic composition.

incompatibleCombinations.message: A steps or scrub scene arranges its own media and beats.
incompatibleCombinations.remediation: Use composition="flow" with scene="steps" or scene="scrub".

incompatibleCombinations.message: A pinned scene and pointer interaction cannot move the same media.
incompatibleCombinations.remediation: Use interaction="none" with scene="steps" or scene="scrub".

contents.description: Generated in-flow links to final primary sections using their exact visible headings.

sticky.description: On a landing: the chapters numbered and held at the edge of a wide screen while the reader scrolls, the current chapter marked; in the flow on a narrow screen and in print.

lead.description: One emphasized opening thesis paragraph inside a section.

muted.description: The quiet continuation of a paragraph in the muted text colour; the sentence before it reads bright: **The run passed.** :muted[Two retries, both on the network step.]

meta.description: A short label in the mono face for identifiers and readings: :meta[run 96 · 01:17].

actions.description: Responsive group containing ordinary action links.

placement.description: Responsive placement for one action inventory.

action.description: Ordinary safe link inside an actions group.

href.description: Safe same-page, relative, HTTP(S), email, phone (tel:), or text-message (sms:) link target; executable and local-file schemes are rejected.

incompatibleCombinations.message: Magnetic action treatment is available only for a primary action.

source-link.description: Source location opened through an explicit IPv4 loopback editor helper without replacing the report page.

label.description: Short visible source path and line.

href.description: IPv4 loopback editor-helper URL with an absolute path and positive source line.

callout.description: Emphasized finding or notice containing Markdown.

source-line.description: The source line under the block before it — which data or footage, how many records, taken when: ::source-line[Moira export of run 96, 212 records]{date="2026-09-25"}.

date.description: When the data or footage was taken: 2026-09-25, or 2026-09-25T01:17 together with zone.

zone.description: IANA time zone of a date with a time, such as Europe/Moscow.

beat.description: One step of a scene="steps" or scene="scrub" section or of a playable demo: Markdown that scrolls past the pinned media or plays in turn; the nth beat shows the nth picture, lights its focus nodes in the diagram or its lines of the code block.

focus.description: Diagram node and connection identities lit while this beat is current, separated by commas; a connection lights when named by its id or when both its nodes are lit.

lines.description: Lines of the code block in the scene lit while this beat is current, such as 3, 2-4 or 1,5-7; the other lines dim.

state.description: Page state set from the moment this beat becomes current; in a scrub scene it stays set for the later beats, so the last beat holds every state of the scene.

count.description: A number in running text that counts up from zero to its written value when it comes into view; the written value is what the page holds and shows without motion.

when.description: Page state that starts the count instead of the number coming into view, such as the chapter that the figure belongs to being reached.

plural.description: A number with its noun in the form the page language requires, settled when the page builds: :plural[5]{forms="file|files"} → 5 files.

forms.description: Noun forms separated by |: English one|other (file|files), Russian one|few|many (файл|файла|файлов).

time.description: A date or a moment written in the page language and, for a time, in a declared time zone, settled when the page builds: :time[2026-09-25T01:17]{zone="Europe/Moscow"}.

zone.description: IANA time zone the time is shown in and named by, such as Europe/Moscow; required when the value has a time.

show.description: What of the moment the page writes: auto (the date, and the time when one is written), date, time or datetime.

swap.description: A word in running text that swaps on a beat to up to three other words and returns to the written one within five seconds; the widest word reserves the width, so the line never moves.

words.description: The other words, separated by commas (one to three); the written label comes first and last.

typing.description: A short line in running text typed in place, character by character, when it comes into view; the whole line is in the page from the start and holds its width, so nothing moves.

mark.description: Words in running text marked by hand: underlined, circled or struck through in the accent colour, drawn when they come into view; the jitter comes from a seed, and a section holds at most two marks.

shape.description: How the words are marked: a hand-drawn underline, a circle around them, or a strike through them.

seed.description: Seed of the hand-drawn jitter (0–9999); the same seed draws the same line. By default it comes from the marked words.

process.description: A mini process in a line of text or a card: its steps, separated by ">" in the label, drawn as dots in order with arcs for the returns and their «×N»; the step names and returns are said in words for assistive technology.

current.description: The step the process stands at, in review; the steps before it are done and the ones after it not started. Without it every step is done.

returns.description: Returns drawn as arcs over the steps, separated by commas, each "step>earlier step×N"; a step returning to itself repeats.

appear.description: Markdown that appears on the next step of its slide in a presentation (layout slides); on any other page, and under reduced motion or in print, it is simply shown.

effect.description: How the content arrives on its step: rising, fading, wiping in from the start edge, or popping.

notes.description: Speaker notes of a slide — a presentation section or a deck slide: never shown to the audience; on a presentation page the presenter view (?view=presenter) shows them under the slide.

deck.description: A slide deck inside the page: slide directives shown one at a time in a 16:9 slot of the column, paged with buttons and keys, and opened on the whole screen; without the runtime and in print the slides follow one another.

id.description: Optional anchor: #id opens the deck, #id/3 opens its third slide.

slide.description: One slide of a deck: Markdown with optional appear steps and speaker notes.

transition.description: How the slide arrives: fade, push from the side, wipe from the start edge, zoom in, or none.

decision.description: Static Markdown decision or typed decision containing decision-option directives.

id.description: Stable identity required when decision options are authored.

required.description: Marks this decision as required in the static document.

decision-option.description: One labelled option inside a typed decision.

checklist.description: Static structured checklist containing stable check-item directives.

check-item.description: One labelled required or optional checklist item.

required.description: Marks this item as required in the static document.

cards.description: Responsive grid, normally containing card directives.

card.description: One semantic card containing Markdown, optionally promoted to one safe whole-card link.

href.description: Safe same-page, relative, HTTP(S), email, phone (tel:), or text-message (sms:) link target; executable and local-file schemes are rejected.

status.description: State label shown on the card as text and a marker: good, watch or risk.

when.description: Page state that lights this card, such as a station that lights when the reader reaches its chapter; until then the card is dimmed. Without motion and in print the card is lit.

steps.description: Process or tutorial sequence containing Markdown, normally an ordered list.

diff.description: One change in unified diff form: exactly one fenced code block with @@ hunks, drawn with old and new line numbers.

file.description: Path of the changed file, shown above the change.

findings.description: Review findings in authored order, with a generated count per severity above them.

finding.description: One review finding with a severity, a title and Markdown detail.

severity.description: How much the finding blocks the change; shown as text, not only colour.

location.description: Where the finding applies, such as a path and line.

conversation.description: A mock of a dialog or a notification feed: message directives in order, with an optional title and an illustrative mark.

illustrative.description: Marks the mock as an illustration: its names, times and numbers are examples, not a record.

message.description: One message or notification: sender, time, Markdown text and an optional status; alone it is a notification, inside conversation it is one turn.

from.description: Sender as the product names it: a person, an agent, a system.

time.description: When it was sent, as the product shows it, such as 01:17 or yesterday.

side.description: in — received, drawn at the start edge; out — sent by the reader, drawn at the end edge.

status.description: Delivery or run status shown under the text, such as delivered or done.

illustrative.description: Marks the mock as an illustration: its names, times and numbers are examples, not a record.

response.description: Local structured reader-response workspace with deterministic export.

question.description: One typed question inside a response workspace.

id.description: Stable question identity within the response form.

step.description: Optional positive increment for number questions.

id.description: Stable bucket identity within the question.
Stable option identity within the question.
Stable item identity within the question.

href.description: Safe same-page, relative, HTTP(S), email, phone (tel:), or text-message (sms:) link target; executable and local-file schemes are rejected.

comment.description: Enables one optional comment for this item.

copyable.description: Ordinary Markdown prose with a localized copy control.

table.description: One Markdown table with a chosen narrow-track layout; a table without the directive uses layout auto.

layout.description: How the table meets a narrow track: auto wraps prose and turns rows into labelled cards only when the columns cannot fit readably; stack turns rows into cards on every narrow track; scroll keeps the grid, scrolls sideways and keeps the first column in view.

glossary.description: Reusable glossary definition containing Markdown, optionally moved from the document root or a direct section child into the appendix.

term.description: Canonical glossary identity and explanation title.

forms.description: Additional declared spellings of the canonical term, comma separated. An occurrence of any declared form counts as an occurrence of the term.

placement.description: Definition location in the authored flow or, from the document root or a direct section child, one package-owned reference appendix.

term.description: Inline or standalone reference that opens a registered glossary explanation. Prose must carry one for the first occurrence of a registered term in each section; later occurrences of that term in the same section stay ordinary prose.

key.description: Key of the glossary definition to reference.

disclosure.description: Native disclosure with a visible summary.

orientation.description: horizontal: the tab list above the panels. vertical: on a wide screen the tab list stands in a column beside the panels (arrow keys up and down move along it); on a narrow screen it returns above them.

modal.description: Modal dialog opened by a package-owned control.

popover.description: Non-modal contextual panel opened by a package-owned control.

filter.description: Client-side text filter for authored list items.

toggle.description: Switch controlling visibility of declarative content.

compare.description: Before and after of the same view: exactly two Markdown images, before then after, laid over each other with a divider the reader moves by pointer or keyboard.

spotlight.description: One screenshot with a loupe over one detail: the detail enlarged in place, the rest of the picture dimmed, and the explanation beside it.

x.description: Horizontal position of the detail, in per cent of the picture width from the left (0–100).

y.description: Vertical position of the detail, in per cent of the picture height from the top (0–100).

zoom.description: How many times the loupe enlarges the detail (1.5–4).

chart.description: Responsive bar, line, or pie chart rendered at compile time.

description.description: Meaningful plain-text description for the visual.

count-up.description: Grow the bars, lines and slices from zero to their values, and count the slice percentages up, when the chart comes into view; under reduced motion and in print the values stand at once.

series.description: One named chart series containing data points.

point.description: One labelled numeric value in a chart series.

diagram.description: Directed flow diagram rendered as deterministic SVG.

description.description: Meaningful plain-text description for the visual.

direction.description: Direction in which flow layers follow each other; auto lets the layout pick the one that reads larger on the page.

layout.description: Flow view shown first and printed: auto picks the clearest; down and right are layered, orthogonal routes at right angles; readers can switch.

spacing.description: Layout breathing room; the package keeps a readable result at every value.

draw.description: Draw the connections as the diagram scrolls through the view, in flow order, with backward connections as a later phase, while a marker rides the connection being drawn; still and complete, the marker at the end, under reduced motion.

pulse.description: A route of node identities separated by commas, each joined to the next by a connection: pulses travel along it three times when the diagram comes into view; under reduced motion the route is marked still.

group.description: One labelled subsystem group around some nodes of a flow diagram.

id.description: Unique group identity within the diagram.

node.description: One labelled node in a flow diagram.

id.description: Unique node identity within the diagram.

detail.description: Optional second line under the label, set smaller: what the node holds or does.

group.description: Optional subsystem group identity; nodes without one stand beside the groups.

kind.description: Package-owned node emphasis; a legend item names what it means.

row.description: Optional one-based flow layer; nodes sharing a row share a layer when their connections allow it.

status.description: Where this step of a process stands: done, review, returned or pending; drawn in the theme status roles with a glyph, named in the legend in package words.

edge.description: One directed connection between diagram nodes; from equal to to is a step that repeats, drawn as a loop on the node in a flow and on the lifeline in a sequence.

to.description: Target node identity; a flow requires a different node.

label.description: Optional connection label, required in a sequence; a long label wraps onto several lines and is never cut.

kind.description: What the connection means; each kind has its own package-drawn line and arrowhead.

route.description: Optional layout pull; direct keeps the connection short and straight, around lets it stretch.

id.description: Optional connection identity, distinct from the node identities: a beat focus lights the connection by it.

count.description: How many times the connection was taken, written «×N» on it: a return repeated, a retry.

legend.description: Optional title and policy for the diagram legend; at most one per diagram.

auto.description: Add the connection kinds the diagram mixes without a legend item of their own.

legend-item.description: One legend entry: names a connection kind, a node emphasis, a node status, or a timeline event emphasis in the author's words, or hides a connection kind.

edge.description: Connection kind this entry names; exclusive with node.

node.description: Node emphasis this entry names; exclusive with edge and requires a label.

status.description: Node status this entry renames in the author's words; exclusive with edge and node.

event.description: Timeline event emphasis this entry names, inside a timeline; requires a label.

label.description: Entry text; a connection kind without one keeps its package name.

hidden.description: Leave this connection kind out of the legend.

zoom.description: The inside of one node of a flow diagram, written as its own small flow: while the diagram is pinned on screen the camera flies into that node and the nested flow grows readable in its place.

node.description: Identity of the node of the enclosing diagram that this flow opens.

timeline.description: Semantic chronological sequence with bounded events.

description.description: Meaningful plain-text description for the visual.

event.description: One dated timeline event with optional Markdown detail.

demo.description: Package-owned demo: a counter card, or with play a scene that reconstructs the product from ordinary directives (code, a diagram, cards, a picture) and plays its beats by time or by scroll; author code is never executed.

step.description: Amount added per activation (counter demo only).

play.description: none: a counter card. time: a playable scene whose beats advance by the page clock, with a play and a pause button, ending on its final frame. scroll: the scene is pinned while the reader scrolls through its beats.

seconds.description: Seconds each beat of a play="time" scene stays current (1–10); the theme pace scales it.

composition.description: A directed, responsive explanation made of named objects and timed actions.

layout.description: Spatial arrangement independent of the scene meaning; rows wrap on compact displays.

align.description: Shared cross-axis alignment; start preserves a common reading edge.

kind.description: Meaning of the composition; layout is package-owned.

object.description: Named Markdown object on a composition stage.

cue.description: One declarative action at a time or speech anchor.

at.description: Seconds or speech anchor b2, b2.end, b2+0.3; standalone beats use three seconds.

slot.description: Local changing slot inside the target object.

toSlot.description: Local changing slot inside the destination object.

emphasis.description: Focus treatment: preserve context by default; dim is explicit, none clears attention.

effect.description: Trace style: moving beam, pulse or packet; follows the connection direction.

scene-group.description: A meaningful group of scene objects with a responsive package-owned arrangement.

layout.description: Spatial arrangement independent of the scene meaning; rows wrap on compact displays.

align.description: Shared cross-axis alignment; start preserves a common reading edge.

slot.description: Named changing value inside a stable object; content is independent of its owner.

id.description: Local value slot inside its stable owner.

asset.description: Download link to a confined local file.

video.description: Embedded local video (webm, mp4, m4v, or ogv), or an agentic-screencast film named by from, as a looping muted clip, a background with a pause control, or a manually started video with sound (the default for a recording that carries sound); directory output ships every source for the browser to choose from, one file ships the most compatible; each source is typed with the codecs read from its file.

src.description: Relative local video path: .webm, .mp4, .m4v, or .ogv. Give the most compatible encoding (H.264 MP4) here. Required unless from names a film.

from.description: A film made by agentic-screencast web: its <film>.web.json manifest, or the directory holding exactly one. The film gives every encoding in the manifest order, the poster, and the chapters; poster, dark-poster, chapters, and sources written here override the film. Use instead of src.

sources.description: Further encodings of the same video, separated by commas, in order of preference (for example AV1 and VP9 from agentic-screencast web); directory output offers all of them before src, one file embeds only the most compatible.

mode.description: clip: muted, looping, plays while visible, with controls. background: muted and looping without controls, with a pause button; a poster is required. manual: starts only when the reader presses play, with sound. Without mode, a recording whose file carries sound (a voice-over; a silent audio track does not count) is manual and a silent one is clip; start, seam="fade", or expand keep it a clip.

chapters.description: Relative WebVTT chapters file (.vtt), such as the one agentic-screencast web writes; the chapters appear as buttons under the video that jump to each chapter.

poster.description: Relative local image shown before playback and in print: .png, .jpg, .jpeg, .webp, .gif, or .avif.

dark-poster.description: Relative local image shown instead of the poster while the page scheme is dark; needs poster, same image types. Print shows the light poster.

caption.description: Visible caption under the video; it also names the video for assistive technology.

start.description: Second of the recording where a looping clip or background starts and every loop returns (0–3600, up to two decimals): the useful part of a recording without re-encoding it.

seam.description: How a looping clip or background joins its end to its start: cut jumps back at once, fade dims the last half-second and brightens the first, so the loop has no visible jump.

expand.description: Adds an Expand button to a clip that opens it large in a dialog with the full player controls and sound.

font.description: Register a confined local font for one text role; the first declaration of each role replaces the theme font of that role.

family.description: CSS font family using letters, numbers, spaces, underscores, or hyphens.

role.description: Text role the font sets: body text and controls, headings and section titles, monospaced labels and metadata, or code blocks and inline code.

each.description: Repeats its Markdown once per item of a list from the page data when the page builds; a body that is one list or one table repeats its items or rows inside it.

in.description: Path of a list in the page data, such as run.blocks.

as.description: Name of the current item inside the body: {{as}} for a plain value, {{as.field}} for a field.

expect.description: A control value over the page data: the build fails at this line when the data at the path diverges from the stated count, bounds or value. Renders nothing.

data.description: Path of the value the expectation reads, such as run.blocks.

count.description: The list at the path has exactly this many items.

min.description: A list has at least this many items (min="1": not empty); a number is at least this value.

max.description: A list has at most this many items; a number is at most this value.

equals.description: A text, number or true/false value written exactly like this.

themes.name: calm-paper
themes.description: Long reading: warm paper, a Playfair display over Literata text, and one clay accent.
themes.palette: Warm paper (#f4f1ea) and dark ink (#1b1a17) for text that reads like print; clay (#ae522d) marks rules and the current place, sage (#3f6b5d) the eyebrows.

themes.name: neutral
themes.description: Neutral reading and product pages: grey paper, a Literata display over Onest, Martian Mono meta lines and JetBrains Mono code, one ochre accent.
themes.palette: Grey paper (#f5f5f3) and ink (#16171a) with one warm ochre accent (#8a5c00); the dark scheme is warm graphite (#151514), not night blue. No cream, no terracotta.

themes.name: frost
themes.description: Two colours and one material: stone grey and graphite, an Onest display over IBM Plex Sans; colour is left to statuses.
themes.palette: Stone (#eef0f3) and graphite (#383e4e) in the light scheme, graphite night (#1b1e25) and stone (#b6bac5) in the dark; the accent is graphite itself, so green, red and ochre appear only as statuses.

themes.name: daylight
themes.description: Product documentation: a bright page, an Onest display over Golos Text, and Geist Mono.
themes.palette: Cool white (#f7f8fa) and graphite ink (#121620); cobalt (#1f5bb8) marks the current place and petrol (#0e6f82) the eyebrows. No default framework palette.

themes.name: midnight
themes.description: Engineering story at night: a Geologica display over IBM Plex Sans, one blue signal and steel for the eyebrows.
themes.palette: Night ink (#0b0e14) with one blue signal (#7aa2ff) and steel (#9fb2c8) for eyebrows; teal stays a chart series only. The light scheme keeps the pair on cool paper.

themes.name: noir
themes.description: Cinematic and editorial: spaced Cormorant Garamond capitals over Jost, amber on black.
themes.palette: Black (#0a0a0b) and bone (#f4f4f5) with amber (#e0a458) and steel (#9fb2c8); the light scheme is ivory with darker amber.

themes.name: aurora
themes.description: Calm research and science: a light Raleway display over Commissioner, one mint signal on deep blue.
themes.palette: Deep blue night (#070b16) with one mint signal (#6fd6c4) and sand (#d9c7a0) for eyebrows; the light scheme is pale sea-green paper with ochre eyebrows.

themes.name: blueprint
themes.description: Dense technical evidence: a Tektur display over Fira Sans, Martian Mono meta lines, cyan and yellow on drafting blue.
themes.palette: Drafting blue (#0a1a33) with cyan (#4cc9f0) and signal yellow (#f9c74f) and a faint grid; the light scheme is blueprint paper.

themes.name: ember
themes.description: Launches and announcements: a condensed Oswald capital page title over Rubik, orange on dark embers.
themes.palette: Ember black (#0e0907) and warm white (#fff4ec) with one orange signal (#ff7a3d) and warm grey (#c9b8a8) for eyebrows; the light scheme is warm paper with burnt orange.

themes.name: synthwave
themes.description: Games and music only: a wide Unbounded display over Exo 2, magenta and cyan on violet night; not for a product landing.
themes.palette: Violet night (#140b27) with magenta (#ff4fd8) and cyan (#37e0ff), for pages whose subject is play or music; the light scheme is lilac paper.

themes.name: terminal
themes.description: Developer console: Martian Mono and JetBrains Mono on graphite or pale console paper, a green prompt, amber labels and a cursor at the page heading.
themes.palette: Console graphite (#0c0e0d) with light grey text (#c9d4cc), one muted green (#5ccf8a) for the prompt and markers and amber (#e0a84a) for labels and focus; the light scheme is pale console paper (#f3f5f1) with deep green (#1d7a45) and dark amber (#8a5a00). Scanlines and glow are off unless the author turns them on.

categories.title: Landing
categories.purpose: Convince a reader to try, adopt or remember something and send them to one next step.

dimensions.question: Which kind of page within the category is this?
Who reads the page, and what do they already know?
What must the reader be able to decide or do after reading?
What real material exists: screenshots, data, code, clips, quotes, documents?
Which languages does the page ship in?
Which visual concept and theme fit the subject and the audience?
How much motion suits the page: none, restrained or expressive?
What does the reader do on the page: only read, filter and switch views, comment (Review Workspace), or answer (Response Workspace)?
How is the page delivered: one file, a published directory, public or private?
Which 5–10 real sites on the same subject were studied before the concepts, and what does each teach?
What does the first screen show: the result, code beside the result, a diagram or a clip?
What is the one action the reader should take?

categories.title: Document
categories.purpose: Explain a finding, a system or a procedure so the reader can check and act on it.

dimensions.question: Which kind of page within the category is this?

What must the reader be able to decide or do after reading?
What real material exists: screenshots, data, code, clips, quotes, documents?
Which languages does the page ship in?
Which visual concept and theme fit the subject and the audience?
How much motion suits the page: none, restrained or expressive?
What does the reader do on the page: only read, filter and switch views, comment (Review Workspace), or answer (Response Workspace)?
How is the page delivered: one file, a published directory, public or private?
Does the reader need the conclusion only, or the full evidence behind it?

fields.name: name
fields.description: Theme identity shown in the theme selector; a theme file defaults to its file name, an inline theme to custom.

fields.name: extends
fields.description: Built-in theme name or relative path to another theme file this theme starts from; defaults to the default theme.

fields.name: description
fields.description: One sentence saying what kind of page the theme is for.

fields.name: palette
fields.description: Why the palette looks the way it does, in words: the named colours and the reason for them.

fields.name: scheme
fields.description: Colour schemes the theme draws: both light and dark, or dark only.

fields.name: accent
fields.description: Named accent family for both schemes; explicit accent colours override it.

fields.name: fonts
fields.description: Type set for the four text roles, or a family per role; the embedded families carry Latin and Cyrillic.

fields.name: pair
fields.description: Coordinated heading, body, label and code families; a family named for a role in the same theme refines it.

fields.name: heading
fields.description: Headings and section titles.

fields.name: body
fields.description: Body text and controls.

fields.name: mono
fields.description: Meta lines, chapter numbers and other monospaced interface text (not code); labels use the body face.

fields.name: code
fields.description: Code blocks and inline code: a text-grade programming face.

fields.name: typography
fields.description: Weight, tracking and leading of the type.

fields.name: headingWeight
fields.description: Weight of headings, 300 to 900.

fields.name: displayWeight
fields.description: Weight of display-size titles, 300 to 900.

fields.name: headingTracking
fields.description: Letter spacing of large headings in Latin text, in em; Cyrillic text never goes tighter than -0.025em.

fields.name: displayCase
fields.description: Letter case of display headings: as written, or capitals that want positive tracking.

fields.name: displayScale
fields.description: Size of display headings against the package scale; wide faces usually look better below 1. Word fit on phones is automatic from the face metrics.

fields.name: headingMeasure
fields.description: Longest line of the page title and of display and editorial section titles, in ch; unset keeps the package measure of each: the reading measure for a report title, 10 to 17ch for landing, first-screen and display titles.

fields.name: bodyLeading
fields.description: Line height of body text.

fields.name: bodyTracking
fields.description: Letter spacing of body text, in em.

fields.name: captions
fields.description: Figure captions and source lines: plain in the text face, or italic in the heading face, the serif italic caption of an editorial page when the heading face is a serif.

fields.name: spacing
fields.description: Density and rhythm of the page.

fields.name: density
fields.description: Shared spacing scale and control padding.

fields.name: rhythm
fields.description: Gap between sections, in rem before density.

fields.name: cardMinimum
fields.description: Narrowest card column, in rem.

fields.name: gap
fields.description: Gap between the navigation column and the content.

fields.name: width
fields.description: Maximum shell width and reading measure.

fields.name: radius
fields.description: Corner treatment of surfaces and controls.

fields.name: radii
fields.description: Which step of the radius scale each role takes: sharp controls with soft cards, square media in a round theme.

fields.name: control
fields.description: Buttons, fields and toolbars; default small.

fields.name: card
fields.description: Cards, panels, dialogs, popovers and stages; default medium.

fields.name: media
fields.description: Images and video on the page; default medium.

fields.name: controls
fields.description: Size of buttons, inputs and actions.

fields.name: backdrop
fields.description: Package-drawn page background in the theme colours.

fields.name: elevation
fields.description: Geometry of raised shadows.

fields.name: motion
fields.description: Character of the package motion: a named curve and a pace for every duration.

fields.name: easing
fields.description: How moving things arrive: standard settles quickly, gentle eases in and out, decisive starts late and lands hard.

fields.name: pace
fields.description: Multiplier of every package duration: brisk, calm (the package timing), or slow.

fields.name: colors
fields.description: Colour roles of each scheme; any role left out comes from the extended theme.

fields.name: light
fields.description: Light scheme colour roles.

fields.name: background
fields.description: Page background. (light scheme)

fields.name: surface
fields.description: Surface of cards, panels and components. (light scheme)

fields.name: raised
fields.description: Raised surface of controls and table headers. (light scheme)

fields.name: muted
fields.description: Muted surface of secondary chips. (light scheme)

fields.name: heading
fields.description: Headings and the fill of primary actions. (light scheme)

fields.name: text
fields.description: Body text. (light scheme)

fields.name: textMuted
fields.description: Secondary text: captions, labels, metadata. (light scheme)

fields.name: border

fields.name: borderStrong
fields.description: Strong borders, lifelines and scrollbars. (light scheme)

fields.name: accent
fields.description: Accent: rules, markers and the current item; drawn, not read as text. (light scheme)

fields.name: accentStrong
fields.description: Strong accent: links and text in accent colour. (light scheme)

fields.name: accentSoft
fields.description: Soft accent: selection and highlight backgrounds. (light scheme)

fields.name: accent2
fields.description: Second accent: eyebrows, kickers and secondary markers. (light scheme)

fields.name: focus
fields.description: Visible keyboard focus ring. (light scheme)

fields.name: chart1

fields.name: chart2
fields.description: Second series colour; the default of statusDone. (light scheme)

fields.name: chart3

fields.name: statusReview

fields.name: statusReturned

fields.name: marker

fields.name: edges
fields.description: Nothing at the screen edges, or small monospace captions along them on a wide screen: the page title on the left, the current chapter and its number on the right — for a technical product.

fields.name: ornaments

fields.name: headingPrefix
fields.description: Up to three characters drawn before the page heading in the accent colour, such as > or §; no spaces, quotes, backslash or <; empty for none.

fields.name: titleCursor
fields.description: Cursor after the page heading: blinks six times, then stays lit; still under reduced motion.

fields.name: heroEmphasis

fields.name: mediaTreatment
fields.description: Plain images, or images with depth and slightly richer colour.

fields.name: console
fields.description: Console details: bracketed labels, dashed rules and a prompt mark at the current contents item.

fields.name: scanlines
fields.description: Faint scanlines over the whole page; off by default, because a texture over the text reads as a generated-site cliché.

fields.name: glow
fields.description: Phosphor glow on headings and the primary action; off by default for the same reason.

fields.name: linkedCard
fields.description: Linked cards raised on hover, or marked by an accent edge.

safety: no author code or template execution

capabilities.live: Explicit loopback hosting with watched source editions, contextual questions, a visible cancellable waiting queue and reader view controls; discussion streams to the existing author Codex session by default, separate agent mode is explicit and ordinary builds remain offline.
capabilities.init: Initialize a packaged declarative starter without overwriting user content.
capabilities.validate: Validate a project through the production preparation pipeline.
capabilities.inspect: Inspect a valid project through the production preparation pipeline.
capabilities.review: Resolve a versioned review artifact to current Markdown source locations.

commands.serve: Serve a local living document attached to the current Codex session; standalone explicitly starts a separate agent, and none watches manual source edits.
commands.init: Initialize a packaged declarative starter without overwriting user content.
commands.validate: Validate a project without writing an output artifact.
commands.inspect: Inspect source usage and the available authoring catalog without writing output.
commands.review: Resolve a confined review artifact without changing report sources.
commands.build: Compile a source into a default or share-safe static artifact.
commands.fix: Apply the replacements the product computed exactly, and nothing else.
commands.theme: Write an author theme file from one or two brand colours, their lightness shifted until every contrast pair passes in both schemes.
commands.schema: Return manifest, directive, or complete source JSON Schema.
commands.examples: List packaged buildable examples and the reference extensions shipped beside them.
commands.sitemap: Write sitemap.xml and robots.txt for a published tree of pages built with a public URL.
commands.snapshot: Build a page and photograph it at several widths, in both schemes, with and without motion, with a contact sheet; with --measure, measure it instead of photographing.
commands.effect-check: Build the examples of an effect extension and run the eleven effect checks in Chromium, reporting N of M checks passed.
